subject: The World Around Us
title: Priya's Water Adventure
hook: Where does rain go? Where does it come from?

slides.title: Following a Water Droplet
slides.storyContext: Priya asks Ravi, 'Have you ever wondered where rainwater goes? Let's follow one water droplet on a magical journey!'

points.label: The journey
points.text: Water evaporates, condenses, precipitates, and returns—over and over!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water travels in a never-ending circle!

image.alt: Following a Water Droplet — Water Cycle

slides.title: A Droplet's Name
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Let's call this water droplet Drippy! Drippy starts in the ocean, minding his own business. Then the sun appears—and that's when his adventure begins!'

points.label: Character setup
points.text: Drippy the water droplet begins in the vast ocean with billions of other water molecules.

slides.inSimpleWords: Meet Drippy, our water droplet hero!

slides.title: The Water Cycle Overview
slides.storyContext: Priya draws a circle on paper. 'The water cycle has four main steps: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, and Collection. Then it starts again! Forever and ever!'

points.label: Four steps
points.text: Evaporation (water rises), Condensation (clouds form), Precipitation (rain falls), Collection (water gathers), then repeat.

slides.inSimpleWords: Four steps, round and round!

slides.title: Evaporation: Water Rises
slides.storyContext: Priya washes clothes in the sun. 'Watch the wet cloth get dry! The sun heats water and turns it invisible. It floats up as vapor!'

points.label: Evaporation
points.text: Sun heats water. Water becomes invisible steam and rises into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sun turns water into invisible steam!

slides.title: Water Evaporates Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees puddles on the road after rain. 'Priya, where do the puddles go?' She smiles. 'The sun evaporates them! See how they disappear?'

example.problem: What happens to puddles on a sunny day?
example.solution: The sun heats them and turns the water into invisible vapor that rises into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Puddles disappear because sun evaporates water!

slides.title: Drippy Rises
slides.storyContext: The sun heats the ocean. Drippy feels warm energy. 'What's happening?' he wonders. His friend Water tells him, 'We're being evaporated! We're turning into invisible vapor and floating upward into the sky!'

points.label: Evaporation begins
points.text: Solar heat provides energy. Water molecules gain energy and escape as vapor.

slides.inSimpleWords: Drippy transforms into invisible vapor and floats up!

slides.title: Heat Energy Powers Evaporation
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Why doesn't water evaporate when it's cold?' Priya explains, 'Heat is the key! The sun's warmth gives energy to water molecules, making them rise.'

points.label: Heat energy
points.text: Evaporation needs energy from the sun. Heat makes water molecules move fast and escape into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: No heat, no evaporation—the sun is the engine!

slides.title: Ocean Water Evaporates Most
slides.storyContext: Priya takes Ravi to a lake and points outward. 'Most water on Earth is in the oceans. Billions of liters evaporate every day from the sun's heat. This is the biggest source of water vapor!'

points.label: Ocean evaporation
points.text: The ocean is Earth's biggest water source. Millions of tons evaporate daily.

slides.inSimpleWords: Oceans give us most of the water vapor in the air!

slides.title: Evaporation Rate
slides.storyContext: Ravi wonders, 'How fast does water evaporate?' Priya says, 'On a hot sunny day, a puddle can vanish in hours. In winter, it takes much longer. Temperature is the key!'

example.problem: Why do puddles disappear faster on hot days than cold days?
example.solution: Hot days provide more solar energy. More energy means faster evaporation. Cold days have less energy, so evaporation is slower.

slides.inSimpleWords: Heat speed = evaporation speed!

slides.title: Condensation: Water Cools
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a cold glass of water on a warm day. 'See these droplets on the outside? Cold air turns vapor back into liquid water!'

points.label: Condensation
points.text: Vapor cools down high in the sky and turns back into tiny water droplets.

slides.inSimpleWords: Cool air turns steam back into water!

slides.title: Drippy's Long Journey Up
slides.storyContext: High in the sky, Drippy floats as invisible vapor. He gets tired, floating higher and higher. 'How much longer?' he sighs. Priya explains, 'He's rising to where it's very cold. Soon he'll meet his friends again!'

points.label: Rising vapor
points.text: Water vapor rises high into the atmosphere, away from the warm surface.

slides.inSimpleWords: Vapor rises higher and higher!

slides.title: Clouds Form
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks up at the sky. Priya explains, 'Those clouds are made of millions of tiny water droplets! They formed when vapor cooled high up!'

example.problem: What are clouds made of?
example.solution: Clouds are millions of tiny water droplets formed when water vapor cools.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clouds are cooled water vapor!

slides.title: Temperature Drop Creates Condensation
slides.storyContext: Priya points upward. 'Water vapor rises higher and higher. The higher up, the colder it gets. When vapor reaches cold air, it condenses and forms clouds!'

points.label: Temperature drop
points.text: Air gets colder as you go higher. At high altitude, vapor hits cold air and condenses.

slides.inSimpleWords: Higher up equals colder equals clouds!

slides.title: Drippy Condenses
slides.storyContext: High in the cold sky, Drippy shivers. 'Brr!' He bumps into other vapor molecules. 'Come together!' says an older droplet. They merge, growing heavier. Drippy becomes visible again—a tiny cloud droplet!

points.label: Condensation moment
points.text: As vapor cools, water molecules slow down and stick together, forming visible liquid droplets.

slides.inSimpleWords: Drippy becomes solid again inside a cloud!

slides.title: Cloud Types Tell Stories
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees fluffy white clouds, thin wispy clouds, and dark gray clouds. Priya says, 'Different clouds mean different weather. Thick dark clouds bring heavy rain!'

points.label: Cloud formation
points.text: Clouds come in different shapes and sizes. Thick clouds hold more water droplets and bring rain.

slides.inSimpleWords: Cloud colors and shapes predict weather!

slides.title: Precipitation: Rain Falls
slides.storyContext: Dark clouds gather. 'Now watch!' says Priya. Rain begins to fall! 'The droplets are so heavy they fall as rain. That's precipitation!'

points.label: Precipitation
points.text: When cloud droplets get too heavy, they fall as rain (or snow, or hail).

slides.inSimpleWords: Heavy droplets fall as rain!

slides.title: Why Rain Falls
slides.storyContext: Ravi wonders, 'Why do clouds suddenly drop rain?' Priya explains, 'Droplets bump into each other and merge, getting heavier. Eventually they're too heavy to float. Gravity pulls them down!'

example.problem: What makes raindrops fall from clouds?
example.solution: Water droplets collide and combine inside clouds, growing heavier until gravity pulls them down as rain.

slides.inSimpleWords: Droplets merge, get heavy, then fall!

slides.title: Different Types of Precipitation
slides.storyContext: Priya explains to Ravi: 'In India, we mostly see rain. But in very cold places, precipitation falls as snow or sleet or hail. It's all water, just in different forms!'

points.label: Precipitation forms
points.text: Rain (warm), snow (freezing), hail (ice pellets), sleet (mixed). All are water falling from clouds.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water falls in many forms depending on temperature!

slides.title: Drippy Falls as Rain
slides.storyContext: Inside the dark cloud, Drippy and trillions of friends have merged into heavy raindrops. They can't float anymore. Down they come! 'Here we go!' shouts Drippy. Splash! Rain pours on Ravi's village!

points.label: Rainfall
points.text: Billions of water droplets fall together as rain, replenishing rivers and soil.

slides.inSimpleWords: Drippy's grand descent begins!

slides.title: Rain on Land
slides.storyContext: Rain pours down. Ravi sees it trickling into the ground, filling wells, ponds, and rivers. 'Where does all this water go?'

example.problem: Where does rainwater go after it falls?
example.solution: Some soaks into the ground (groundwater), some flows into rivers and ponds, some is drunk by plants and animals.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain soaks into ground and fills rivers!

slides.title: Water Soaks Deep
slides.storyContext: Priya kneels in wet soil. 'Some rain doesn't stay on the surface. It soaks down through soil and rock. This becomes groundwater—water that plants and underground streams use!'

points.label: Infiltration
points.text: Rainwater soaks into soil and rock, becoming groundwater. It fills wells and aquifers.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain sinks into Earth's deep ground!

slides.title: Collection: Water Gathers
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a well, a pond, and the river. 'Look! All this water came from rain. It collects here, waiting to be used.'

points.label: Collection
points.text: Rainwater collects in wells, rivers, lakes, and oceans—the water cycle starts again!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water collects in rivers and ponds!

slides.title: Groundwater to Plants
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees plant roots going deep into soil. Priya explains, 'Plant roots drink groundwater! They pull it up from underground to grow and make leaves. This water will eventually evaporate too!'

example.problem: How do plants get water in dry seasons?
example.solution: Plant roots extend deep underground to reach groundwater. They absorb it and use it to grow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants drink groundwater through their roots!

slides.title: Transpiration: Plants Release Water
slides.storyContext: Priya points to leaves glistening in the morning sun. 'Plants don't just store water. They release water vapor through tiny holes in leaves called stomata. This is called transpiration!'

points.label: Transpiration
points.text: Plants absorb groundwater and release water vapor through leaves. This vapor goes back into the atmosphere!

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants release water vapor into the air!

slides.title: Drippy in the Well
slides.storyContext: Drippy lands in Ravi's village well. 'Another adventure!' he thinks. Ravi's family draws water from the well. 'Drippy is giving us life-giving water!' Ravi declares. But Drippy's journey isn't over—the cycle continues forever.

points.label: Drippy's pause
points.text: Water collects in wells and is used by humans, but it will evaporate again and again.

slides.inSimpleWords: Even used water will cycle again!

slides.title: The Complete Cycle
slides.storyContext: Priya draws a circle. 'Evaporation → Condensation → Precipitation → Collection → Evaporation again! It never stops!'

points.label: Cycle
points.text: The water cycle is continuous and endless.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water goes round and round forever!

slides.title: Cycle Challenge: Label Each Step
slides.storyContext: Priya gives Ravi a challenge: 'I'll describe each step. You name it! (1) Water vapor rises. (2) Clouds form. (3) Rain falls. (4) Water collects in rivers.' Ravi correctly answers: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Collection!

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Can you name each stage of the water cycle?

slides.inSimpleWords: Four stages, five words: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Collection, Repeat!

slides.title: Same Water, Always
slides.storyContext: Ravi realizes, 'So the rain that falls today might have been in this well before!' Priya nods. 'Yes! Same water, recycled forever!'

example.problem: Is the water we drink the same water from millions of years ago?
example.solution: Yes! Earth's water is recycled endlessly through the water cycle.

slides.inSimpleWords: Same water gets reused forever!

slides.title: Water Journey Ends
slides.storyContext: That night, Ravi watches the rain. He now knows each droplet's journey—up, into clouds, down as rain, and starting again!

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Evaporation: Sun heats water into vapor. 2. Condensation: Vapor cools into droplets. 3. Precipitation: Droplets fall as rain. 4. Collection: Water gathers in rivers/ponds. 5. The cycle repeats forever! 6. All water is recycled. 7. Plants help the cycle via transpiration. 8. We must protect this precious cycle.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water cycles through evaporation, clouds, and rain!

subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi and Priya's Healthy Plate
hook: Which foods make us strong and which make us sick?

slides.title: Mummy's Kitchen Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi comes home tired. His mother makes him a meal with rice, beans, vegetables, and fruit. Priya visits and says, 'Your mom is teaching you about healthy eating!'

points.label: The meal
points.text: Different foods give different nutrients to our body.

slides.inSimpleWords: Healthy food gives us energy and strength!

slides.title: Energy for Playing
slides.storyContext: Ravi is too tired to play cricket. Priya asks, 'Did you eat breakfast?' He shakes his head. 'That's the problem! Food is fuel for your body, just like petrol for a car. No fuel, no energy!'

points.label: Food as fuel
points.text: Food gives energy to run, play, think, and grow. Without food, we feel tired.

slides.inSimpleWords: Food is fuel for our bodies!

slides.title: What is Nutrition?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Our food breaks down into tiny nutrients—proteins, carbs, fats, vitamins, minerals, water. Each does a special job in our body!'

points.label: Nutrients
points.text: Carbs give energy. Proteins build muscles. Fats store energy. Vitamins and minerals keep us healthy.

slides.inSimpleWords: Different nutrients do different jobs in our body!

slides.title: Six Main Food Groups
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a chart: Grains, Proteins, Vegetables, Fruits, Dairy, and Fats. 'Every food belongs to one of these groups. Each group has special powers!'

points.label: Food groups
points.text: Grains (energy), Proteins (growth), Vegetables (vitamins), Fruits (immunity), Dairy (bones), Healthy Fats (brain).

slides.inSimpleWords: Six food groups, six superpowers!

slides.title: Grains for Energy
slides.storyContext: Priya points to rice and bread. 'These are grains. They give your body energy so you can run, play, and study hard!'

points.label: Grains
points.text: Rice, wheat, bread, roti—give energy and strength.

slides.inSimpleWords: Grains give us energy to play!

slides.title: Carbohydrates Explained
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Priya, how do grains give energy?' She explains, 'Grains have carbohydrates. When you eat them, your body breaks them down into glucose—sugar that becomes instant energy!'

example.problem: How does eating rice give us energy?
example.solution: Rice contains carbohydrates. Our body breaks them down into glucose, which enters our blood and powers our muscles and brain.

slides.inSimpleWords: Carbs turn into sugar that powers us!

slides.title: Protein for Growing
slides.storyContext: Priya shows beans, eggs, and paneer. 'These have protein. Protein helps you grow tall and makes your muscles strong!'

points.label: Protein
points.text: Beans, eggs, milk, yogurt, paneer, fish—build muscles and make you grow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Protein helps us grow tall and strong!

slides.title: Building Blocks
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches a construction site. Priya points, 'See how workers stack bricks? Protein builds your body the same way! Each protein molecule is a brick in your muscles and bones.'

example.problem: Why do growing children need protein?
example.solution: Protein provides amino acids that build muscle tissue, bone, and other body structures. Growing kids need lots of it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Protein builds muscles and bones!

slides.title: Vegetables for Vitamins
slides.storyContext: Priya holds green leafy vegetables, orange carrots, red tomatoes. 'Each color gives different vitamins. Green keeps eyes healthy, orange is good for seeing!'

points.label: Vegetables
points.text: Carrots, spinach, tomatoes, peas—full of vitamins and minerals.

slides.inSimpleWords: Colorful veggies keep us healthy!

slides.title: Rainbow Vegetables
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Ravi: 'Green veggies have folate for blood. Orange has beta-carotene for eyes. Red has lycopene for heart. Eat the rainbow!'

points.label: Color equals nutrients
points.text: Each color vegetable has unique vitamins. Eating many colors keeps all body parts healthy.

slides.inSimpleWords: Colorful vegetables give different health benefits!

slides.title: Key Vitamins and Minerals
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a chart. 'Vitamin A helps eyes. Vitamin C helps immunity. Iron helps blood. Calcium helps bones. All found in different vegetables!'

points.label: Key nutrients
points.text: Vitamin A (carrots, spinach), Vitamin C (tomatoes, peppers), Iron (spinach), Calcium (milk, greens).

slides.inSimpleWords: Each vitamin does a special job!

slides.title: Fruits for Immunity
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats an apple and banana. Priya explains, 'Fruits have vitamins that keep you from getting sick. Eat different colored fruits!'

example.problem: Why should we eat fruits daily?
example.solution: Fruits have vitamins that boost immunity and prevent sickness. Oranges have vitamin C, bananas have potassium.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits keep our bodies strong!

slides.title: Natural Sweets vs Junk Sweets
slides.storyContext: Ravi wants to eat candy. Priya offers him a banana. 'Both are sweet, but banana has fiber, potassium, and vitamins. Candy has only sugar and empty calories. Banana is smarter!'

points.label: Better choices
points.text: Natural sweets (fruits) have nutrients. Candy and sweets have only sugar.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits are sweet AND healthy!

slides.title: Dairy for Bones
slides.storyContext: Priya pours milk. 'Milk, yogurt, and paneer have calcium. Calcium makes your bones and teeth strong and healthy!'

points.label: Dairy
points.text: Milk, yogurt, cheese—calcium for strong bones and teeth.

slides.inSimpleWords: Milk makes bones strong!

slides.title: Calcium in Detail
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Why is calcium so important?' Priya explains, 'Calcium makes bones hard and strong. Without it, bones become weak and crack easily. Kids need lots of calcium to build strong bones for life!'

example.problem: What happens if kids don't drink milk?
example.solution: Without calcium, bones become weak. They may break easily or curve. Adults who had calcium-poor childhoods suffer bone diseases.

slides.inSimpleWords: Calcium is the skeleton's best friend!

slides.title: Healthy Fats and Oils
slides.storyContext: Priya opens a small bottle of sesame oil. 'Some fats are healthy! Nuts, seeds, and oils help our brain and heart. But too much fried food is bad.'

points.label: Good fats
points.text: Healthy fats from nuts, seeds, fish, olive oil—help brain and heart. Avoid too much fried food.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some fats are healthy if you don't overeat!

slides.title: Making a Healthy Plate
slides.storyContext: Priya and Ravi draw a plate. 'Half should be vegetables and fruits. One quarter grains. One quarter protein. Plus milk!' A perfect healthy meal!

points.label: Plate model
points.text: Half: veggies/fruits. Quarter: grains. Quarter: protein. Plus dairy.

slides.inSimpleWords: A healthy plate is colorful and balanced!

image.alt: Making a Healthy Plate — Healthy Food

slides.title: Proportions Matter
slides.storyContext: Ravi makes a plate with only rice. Priya shakes her head. 'Not balanced! You need vegetables for vitamins, protein to grow, and fruit for immunity. All together in right portions!'

points.label: Balance
points.text: Each meal should have all food groups in the right amounts.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat a rainbow on every plate!

slides.title: Unhealthy vs Healthy
slides.storyContext: Priya shows two meals. 'This one has candy, chips, soda—lots of sugar. Not good! This one has rice, vegetables, lentils—much better!'

example.problem: Why is candy unhealthy?
example.solution: Candy has too much sugar and not enough nutrients. Eating too much makes teeth bad and causes sickness.

slides.inSimpleWords: Too much sugar and junk food makes us sick!

slides.title: Water for Hydration
slides.storyContext: Priya fills a glass with water. 'Water is the most important drink! Drink plenty daily to stay healthy. It's better than sugary juices!'

points.label: Water
points.text: Drink 6-8 glasses of water daily. Water is best for health!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water is the healthiest drink!

slides.title: Why Hydration Matters
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Our bodies are 60% water! Water carries nutrients, removes waste, keeps joints moving, and helps digestion. Dehydration makes us tired and sick.'

points.label: Body's water
points.text: Water makes up most of our body. It's essential for every function.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water runs our entire body!

slides.title: Ravi's Healthy Day
slides.storyContext: Breakfast: oats and milk. Lunch: rice, dal, vegetables. Snack: apple and yogurt. Dinner: roti and paneer. 'This day will keep me strong!' says Ravi.

points.label: Sample day
points.text: Eating healthy at every meal keeps energy high and body strong.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eating healthy all day keeps us strong!

slides.title: Portion Sizes Matter
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats too much rice. Priya explains, 'Even healthy food in huge amounts makes you overweight. Portions must be right—not too little, not too much!'

points.label: Control portions
points.text: Healthy eating includes eating the right amount, not just the right foods.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat healthy foods in healthy amounts!

slides.title: Sugar and Salt: The Dangers
slides.storyContext: Priya warns Ravi: 'Too much sugar causes obesity and dental cavities. Too much salt raises blood pressure. Keep both to minimum!'

points.label: Excess nutrients
points.text: Sugar damages teeth and causes weight gain. Salt can damage heart and kidneys. Limit both.

slides.inSimpleWords: Too much sugar and salt hurts our health!

slides.title: Digestion: Food's Journey
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'When you swallow food, it travels down into your stomach and intestines. Your body breaks it down into tiny nutrients that enter your blood.'

points.label: Digestion process
points.text: Food enters mouth, travels to stomach, then intestines. Nutrients are absorbed into blood.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body turns food into fuel!

slides.title: Fiber for Digestion
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats an apple with skin. Priya says, 'Fiber in vegetables, fruits, and grains helps your digestion move smoothly. It's like a broom for your intestines!'

points.label: Fiber
points.text: Found in vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. Helps digestion and keeps you regular.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fiber is nature's digestive broom!

slides.title: Read a Food Label
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a cereal box. 'Look here—calories, carbs, protein, fiber. Understanding labels helps you choose healthier foods!'

example.problem: How do we know if a food is healthy?
example.solution: Check the label! Look for low sugar, high fiber, and nutrients. Compare similar products.

slides.inSimpleWords: Food labels tell us what's inside!

slides.title: Snacking Smart
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Ravi: 'Snacks can be healthy! Nuts, yogurt, fruit are good snacks. Chips and candy are not. Smart snacking keeps energy steady between meals.'

points.label: Healthy snacks
points.text: Nuts, fruit, yogurt, cheese—give lasting energy. Avoid sugary and fried snacks.

slides.inSimpleWords: Snack smart, stay strong!

slides.title: Healthy Food Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi now understands: every food has a job. Grains for energy, proteins for growth, veggies for health, fruits for immunity, water for life!

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Grains = energy. 2. Proteins = growth. 3. Vegetables = vitamins. 4. Fruits = immunity. 5. Dairy = strong bones. 6. Healthy fats = brain. 7. Water = hydration. 8. Fiber = digestion. 9. Eat colorful, balanced meals! 10. Control portions. 11. Limit sugar and salt. 12. Healthy eating = healthy life!

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat healthy to grow strong and happy!

subject: English
title: Priya's Mystery Adventure
hook: Help Priya understand stories by asking the right questions

slides.title: Reading Comprehension
slides.storyContext: Priya sits with her grandmother in their village home. The monsoon rain taps on the roof. Daadiji opens an old book of folktales.
slides.inSimpleWords: Learning to understand and enjoy the stories you read.

slides.title: The Mystery of the Lost Parrot
slides.storyContext: One morning, Priya reads a story in her textbook: 'Karan found a colorful parrot sitting on his window. He gave it water and seeds. The next day, the parrot flew away and brought a friend. Now Karan had two parrots.'
slides.inSimpleWords: A story is like a gift—read it slowly, watch what happens, and think about why.

image.alt: The Mystery of the Lost Parrot — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Reading is a Skill
slides.storyContext: Daadiji explains to Priya: 'Reading is not just pronouncing words. It's understanding what the author is saying, seeing pictures in your mind, and feeling the story.'

points.text: Reading = recognizing words + understanding meaning + enjoying the story

slides.inSimpleWords: Good reading means truly understanding the story!

slides.title: Who, What, Where, When
slides.storyContext: Daadiji asks Priya questions about the parrot story. Priya learns to spot the main details.

points.label: Who
points.text: The people or animals in the story (Karan and the parrots)

points.label: What
points.text: What happens in the story (a parrot visits, then brings a friend)

points.label: Where
points.text: Where the story takes place (on Karan's window)

points.label: When
points.text: The time of the story (morning, then next day)

slides.inSimpleWords: Always ask these 4 questions to understand any story.

image.alt: Who, What, Where, When — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Who and What Practice
slides.storyContext: Priya reads a new story: 'Meera and her dog Tippy went to the park. They played fetch all afternoon. Tippy caught the ball every time!'

example.problem: Who is the story about and what do they do?
example.solution: WHO: Meera and her dog Tippy. WHAT: They go to the park and play fetch.

slides.inSimpleWords: Always find who and what first!

slides.title: The Main Idea
slides.storyContext: Sunny barks at a lizard on the wall. Priya thinks: 'This is a small detail. The BIG idea in the parrot story is: kindness brings friendship.'

points.text: A story has a main idea—the most important thing that happens
Small details support the main idea (Karan gave water and seeds)
The main idea teaches us something (be kind to animals)

slides.inSimpleWords: The main idea is like the heart of the story; everything else supports it.

slides.title: Finding the Main Idea
slides.storyContext: Daadiji asks Priya: 'In the Meera story, what is the main idea?' Priya thinks: 'Meera loves her dog very much. They have fun together.' Daadiji nods. 'That's the heart!'

example.problem: What is the main idea of the Meera story?
example.solution: The main idea is that Meera and Tippy share a strong bond and love playing together. The specific detail (playing fetch) supports this big idea.

slides.inSimpleWords: Main idea equals the most important message!

slides.title: Finding the Order of Events
slides.storyContext: Priya uses three stones to mark: First stone (Karan finds parrot), middle stone (he gives food), last stone (parrot brings a friend). This is the order things happen.

points.text: Events happen in order: first, then, finally
Words like 'morning', 'next day', 'then' show order
Knowing the order helps you understand the story better

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories move forward like steps up a ladder—one thing after another.

image.alt: Finding the Order of Events — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Story Sequencing
slides.storyContext: Priya learns to spot order words: 'Once', 'Then', 'Next', 'Finally', 'Meanwhile', 'At last'. These words tell her when things happen. Without order, stories become confusing!

points.text: Order words are clues. They show the story's timeline.

slides.inSimpleWords: Order words guide us through the story!

slides.title: Understanding Feelings
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: 'How did Karan feel when the parrot came back with a friend?' Daadiji smiles: 'His heart was full of joy! He loved the animals even more.'

points.text: Characters have feelings (happy, sad, scared, excited)
We know their feelings from what they DO (Karan gave food equals he cares)
Understanding feelings helps us like the story more

slides.inSimpleWords: Good readers feel what the characters feel.

slides.title: Feelings from Actions
slides.storyContext: Daadiji reads: 'Asha saw her mother crying. She ran and hugged her tight. She brought her a glass of water and sat beside her.' Priya says, 'Asha must love her very much!'

example.problem: How do we know Asha's feelings if the author doesn't say them?
example.solution: From her actions! She hugs her mother, brings water, and sits beside her. These actions show love and care.

slides.inSimpleWords: Actions reveal character feelings!

slides.title: Cause and Effect
slides.storyContext: Priya learns: 'WHY did the parrot fly away? BECAUSE Karan was kind. That's cause and effect—why something happens.'

points.text: Cause equals WHY something happens
Effect equals WHAT happens as a result
Understanding cause-effect makes stories make sense

slides.inSimpleWords: Cause is why; effect is what happens!

slides.title: Read and Answer
slides.storyContext: Daadiji gives Priya a short story to practice: 'Meera went to the market with her mother. She saw a stall with colorful ribbons. She chose a blue ribbon for her sister's hair. Her sister danced with joy.'

example.problem: Read the story and tell: (1) Who is the main person? (2) What did Meera do? (3) Where did it happen? (4) How did Meera's sister feel?
example.solution: (1) Meera. (2) She went to the market and bought a blue ribbon. (3) At the market. (4) Happy and joyful—she danced!

slides.inSimpleWords: Always ask WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN to answer questions about stories.

slides.title: Details vs Main Idea
slides.storyContext: Priya struggles. She writes down every tiny detail: 'Karan wore red shirt. The window had blue paint. The parrot was green.' Daadiji says, 'Those are nice details, but what's the MAIN point?' Priya realizes: 'Kindness brings friends!'

points.text: Details equal small facts. Main idea equals big message.

slides.inSimpleWords: Keep the main idea central; details support it!

slides.title: Your Turn: Mini Story
slides.storyContext: Priya's teacher gives her a short passage: 'Ram liked to play cricket. One day, he broke the ball. He felt sad. But his friend Asha gave him a new ball. Ram was very happy. They played together until sunset.'

example.problem: Answer: (1) What was the problem? (2) How was it solved? (3) What is the main idea?
example.solution: (1) Ram broke his ball. (2) Asha gave him a new ball. (3) Real friends help when we are sad.

slides.inSimpleWords: Read carefully, ask questions, and think about what the story teaches.

image.alt: Your Turn: Mini Story — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Practice Passage: The Lost Bicycle
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'Rahul lost his bicycle keys. He looked everywhere for an hour. He felt worried. Then his neighbor Mr. Khan found the keys under a bush. He returned them to Rahul. Rahul thanked him with a smile.'

example.problem: Answer: (1) Who? (2) What problem? (3) Where? (4) Main idea?
example.solution: (1) Rahul and Mr. Khan. (2) Lost bicycle keys. (3) Rahul's neighborhood. (4) Kindness of neighbors helps in time of need.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice asking all the questions!

slides.title: Inferencing: Reading Between Lines
slides.storyContext: Daadiji says: 'Sometimes authors don't say everything. We must INFER—guess what they mean based on clues.' Priya reads: 'Ravi's eyes were wet. His voice was shaky.' Priya infers, 'He must be sad or scared.'

points.text: Inference equals using clues to guess what isn't said
Good readers use text clues plus their own experience

slides.inSimpleWords: Read between the lines to understand deeper meaning!

slides.title: Inference Practice
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'Manju hadn't eaten all day. Her mother made her favorite khichdi. Manju's nose twitched. A smile spread across her face.' Priya infers: 'Manju was hungry and happy to see her favorite food!'

example.problem: What can we infer about Manju from the clues?
example.solution: She was hungry (hadn't eaten all day). She was happy and excited (nose twitched, smiled). She loves khichdi (mother made her favorite).

slides.inSimpleWords: Clues help us infer character feelings and situations!

slides.title: Vocabulary from Context
slides.storyContext: Priya encounters a new word: 'The old castle stood majestically on the hill, its grand towers reaching toward the sky.' She guesses, 'Majestically means impressively or beautifully, because castles are impressive places.'

points.text: When you see a new word, look at other words around it for clues
Context helps you guess the meaning without a dictionary

slides.inSimpleWords: Context clues help you understand new words!

slides.title: Preview Before Reading
slides.storyContext: Daadiji teaches Priya: 'Before you read, preview! Look at the title, pictures, and first sentence. This gives you clues about what the story will be.'

points.text: Previewing helps prepare your mind for the story.

slides.inSimpleWords: Preview like peeking at a gift before opening!

slides.title: Summarizing a Story
slides.storyContext: After reading, Priya summarizes: 'The story is about Karan who was kind to a parrot, and it brought him friendship.' That's a summary—the main points in your own words.

points.text: Summary = main idea + key events in fewer words

slides.inSimpleWords: A summary is the story in a nutshell!

slides.title: Story Summary Practice
slides.storyContext: Daadiji reads a story about a girl who plants a seed, watches it grow, and shares the flowers. Priya summarizes: 'A girl's kindness (planting a gift) brings joy to her community (sharing flowers).'

example.problem: Summarize this story in 1-2 sentences.
example.solution: A girl plants a seed with love and care. The flowers that grow bring happiness to everyone around her.

slides.inSimpleWords: Summaries capture the heart of the story!

slides.title: Compare and Contrast Stories
slides.storyContext: Priya reads two stories: one about Karan with a parrot, one about Meera with her dog. Daadiji asks, 'How are they alike? Different?' Priya sees both are about kindness, but different animals.

points.text: Comparing = finding similarities. Contrasting = finding differences.

slides.inSimpleWords: See how stories are same and different!

slides.title: Fiction vs Non-Fiction
slides.storyContext: Daadiji shows Priya two books. 'This one has imaginary animals talking—that's fiction. This one teaches real facts about animals—that's non-fiction. Different types, different purposes!'

points.text: Fiction = made-up stories. Non-fiction = real facts.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fiction is imaginary; non-fiction is real!

slides.title: Write Your Own Story
slides.storyContext: Daadiji challenges Priya: 'Now YOU write a story! Remember: have characters, setting, events, and a main idea. Make it interesting!' Priya writes about Sunny helping a lost child find home.

example.problem: Can you create your own story with characters and a main idea?
example.solution: Yes! Your story should have: WHO (characters), WHERE (setting), WHAT (plot), and a main idea (message or lesson).

slides.inSimpleWords: You can be an author too!

slides.title: How to Understand Stories

points.text: Ask WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN to find key details
Find the main idea—what the story is really about
Notice the order of events (first, then, finally)
Understand how characters feel through their actions
Look for cause and effect (why things happen)
Infer meaning from clues when author doesn't say it
Use context to understand new words
Preview before reading and summarize after
Good readers ask questions and think deeply

slides.inSimpleWords: Reading is like detective work—look for clues and understand the whole picture!
